title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-notes
content:
Top-level goal: interactive debugging breadcrumbs for Dedicated GPU pool autoscale/warmup thrash (Jan 10-12). Raw scratchpad for follow-ups.

High-level summary:
- Observed oscillation: nodes created -> pods scheduled -> image pulls/readiness fail -> nodes cordoned/drained -> autoscaler spins new nodes -> repeat.
- Likely root causes: slow image pulls on new AMI/containerd combo, aggressive autoscaler health checks, taint/toleration timing mismatch, and possible registry throttling under parallel scale-ups.

Key observed symptoms & metrics:
- p95 request latency up from ~110ms -> ~2.4s during peak thrash windows.
- Node creation latency: ~85s cloud boot + 30-90s container warmup; total ~2-3 minutes to serve traffic.
- Autoscaler churn: 12 scale-up events in an ~8 minute window (2025-01-11 03:12-03:20 UTC).
- Events in cluster: many ImagePullBackOff, FailedScheduling (Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu), Readiness probe timeouts, NodeNotReady and cordon events correlated with scale-ups.

Timestamped interactive breadcrumbs (trimmed):
- 2025-01-11 03:14 UTC: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep model-x
  model-x-5d9c8    0/1 Pending    0          10s
- 2025-01-11 03:14 UTC: kubectl describe pod model-x-5d9c8 -n redwood-serving
  Events:
    - 03:14:10 PodScheduled
    - 03:14:11 FailedScheduling: 0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
    - 03:14:20 Normal Scheduled
    - 03:14:20 Pulling image "registry.redwood.internal/model-runtime:gpu-v3"
    - 03:14:40 Failed to pull image: context deadline exceeded
    - 03:15:20 Readiness probe failed (timeout)
    - 03:15:25 Node became NotReady and was cordoned by cluster-autoscaler

- 2025-01-11 03:16 UTC: kubectl get nodes | grep dedicated-gpu
  dedicated-gpu-12 Ready  3d  (taints: gpu-prewarm=true:NoSchedule)
  dedicated-gpu-13 NotReady 5s

- Cluster-autoscaler logs (recent 15m):
  "scale_up: adding node (dedicated-gpu-14)"
  "scale_up: delay scaling SCALEDOWN disabled because of busy nodes"
  "scale_up: failed to mark node as healthy: readiness probe timed out"

- Cloud inventory: recent nodes are g5.2xlarge; older warm nodes were g5.8xlarge. Some node AMIs differ (image-2024-12 vs image-20241208). Correlation: older AMI had faster pulls.

Hypotheses (ordered by perceived likelihood):
1) AMI/container runtime mismatch: newer AMI/containerd combo has slower image pulls (no cache) causing prewarm containers to miss readiness windows -> nodes marked unhealthy -> oscillation.
2) Taint/toleration lifecycle issue: prewarm daemonsets set gpu-prewarm=true:NoSchedule and remove taint only after image pull success; serving pods lack toleration so prewarm nodes are idle and autoscaler drains/creates more.
3) Autoscaler health thresholds too aggressive: nodes marked unhealthy on first readiness failure instead of after retries.
4) Traffic pattern amplification: many tiny cold-start requests spawn short-lived pods causing frequent scale events.
5) Registry-side throttling: image registry returns 429s/timeout under many parallel pulls leading to repeated failures.

Actions taken so far (results):
- Rolled back test pool to previous AMI (ami-20241208) -> image pulls ~3x faster; prewarm succeeds. Supports hypothesis #1.
- Increased readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds for prewarm container 10->30s -> fewer immediate cordons, but still failures during parallel boots.
- Patched serving deployment with toleration for gpu-prewarm=true:NoSchedule -> pods could land on prewarm nodes but caused resource contention. Not ideal long-run.
- Tuned autoscaler config in test cluster: increased node-group "unhealthyAfter" from 30s->2m -> reduced thrash but slowed removal of truly bad nodes.
- Enabled pull-through cache on some registry frontends -> registry 429s reduced in load tests.

Open checks and experiments to run next:
- Repro test: synthetic cold-burst (100 concurrent cold requests) vs pool with old AMI and new AMI to measure image-pull/warmup differences and p95 latency. Priya assigned.
- Compare container runtimes between AMIs: containerd version, docker shim, overlayfs/backing fs -- list binaries and versions on both images.
- Audit who injects gpu-prewarm taint (admission controllers/daemonset) and the exact remove timing; add audit logs. Mateo assigned.
- Autoscaler behavior: can we change to require N consecutive readiness failures before marking node unhealthy? Check safety/side-effects.
- Registry metrics: correlate 5xx/429s with incident window (work with registry/infra team).

Short-term mitigations proposed:
- Pin Dedicated pool to older AMI (ami-20241208) with proven warmup speed until a fix is in place. (fastest mitigation to reduce customer impact)
- Increase readinessProbe timeouts and autoscaler unhealthy thresholds cluster-wide for Dedicated pools where acceptable.
- Add a small "fast-warm" pool (smaller instances with cached images) to soak bursts and offload cold-starts.

Longer-term improvements to consider:
- Bake image cache into AMI or ensure container runtime pulls from a local cache on boot.
- Make prewarm process responsible for removing taints only after image+model warm succeed.
- Improve autoscaler health logic: tolerate a couple of probe failures before cordoning; add exponential backoff.
- Introduce a lightweight init actor that pre-pulls images and warms models independent of main pod lifecycle (faster startup).

Owners / next steps:
- @Priya Kumar: run synthetic cold-burst experiments comparing AMIs (assigned).
- @Mateo Alvarez: audit taint injection path & patch admission controller logging (assigned).
- @Infra team: evaluate AMI bake changes and local registry cache on boot.

Useful links/logs:
- JIRA-INC-2345 (incident doc)
- slack:#serving-runtime thread-CK2M8J9 (investigation)
- github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (autoscaler tweak)

Slack-ready summary (one-liner):
"Autoscaler / node warmup oscillation observed during cold bursts. Likely root cause: slow image pulls on new AMI + aggressive autoscaler health checks. Short-term: pin pool to older AMI and raise unhealthy thresholds; running synthetic tests to validate."

Notes: this is a scratchpad (unreviewed). Keep iterations here until we have a formal postmortem draft.
